plan.title: 3' tag-seq DESeq2 DE: treated vs control liver
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 6 samples) from a Lexogen QuantSeq 3' tag-seq experiment in human liver, 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. Because it is a 3' tag library, gene counts do not depend on transcript length, so no length-normalized unit (TPM/FPKM) or tximport step applies; raw integer counts go directly into DESeq2. The plan follows the grounded procedure: (1) sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) including a check that the declared 3' strand protocol matches what the data show, since strandedness is declared but unverified; (2) a minimal low-count pre-filter using a lowered floor (>=5 counts, appropriate for 3' tag data per R-0080) in at least the smallest group size (3) of samples, leaving DESeq2's independent filtering to do the rest; (3) DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization and a ~condition design with an explicit reference level (control) and named contrast (treated vs control), plus a GC-content bias diagnostic (no length bias expected for 3' tag data) and an explicit statement of the expected power at n=3/group; (4) DESeq2 Wald test differential expression with apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change, reporting both shrunken and unshrunken estimates; (5) BH multiple-testing correction with independent filtering at alpha=0.05, with a p-value histogram diagnostic; (6) fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (human, 2026.1), followed by Reactome and WikiPathways human collections, all present in the reference store; (7) a final report consolidating fit diagnostics, gene tables, the replicate-power caveat (n=3/group is low power, absence of a gene from the DE list is not evidence of no effect), enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions, seeds).

steps.method: vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size QC

Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, alpha=0.05
fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald statistic vs MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways
Reproducible report with MA/dispersion plots, gene tables, power caveat, enrichment tables
